recipes.name: Old Fashioned Peach Cobbler
ingredients_raw: 3 pounds fresh peaches - peeled, pitted, and sliced

steps.text: To make the crust: Sift flour, 3 tablespoons sugar, and salt together in a medium bowl. Work in shortening with a pastry blender until mixture resembles coarse crumbs.
Whisk egg and cold water together in a small bowl. Sprinkle over flour mixture; work with hands to form dough into a ball. Wrap with plastic wrap and chill in the refrigerator for 30 minutes.
Preheat the oven to 350 degrees F (175 degrees C). Roll out 1/2 of the chilled dough to 1/8-inch thickness.
Place in a 9x13-inch baking dish, covering the bottom and halfway up the sides. Bake in the preheated oven until golden brown, about 20 minutes.
To make the filling: Mix peaches, orange juice, and lemon juice in a large saucepan. Add butter and cook over medium-low heat until butter is melted.
Stir sugar, cornstarch, cinnamon, and nutmeg together in a bowl; mix into peach mixture until combined. Pour into baked crust.
Roll remaining dough to 1/4-inch thickness. Cut into 1/2-inch-wide strips.
Weave strips into a lattice over peaches. Sprinkle with 1 tablespoon sugar, then drizzle with melted butter.
Bake in the preheated oven until top crust is golden brown, 35 to 40 minutes.

raw_recipe.headline: Old Fashioned Peach Cobbler
raw_recipe.description: This old-fashioned peach cobbler recipe features flaky, homemade pastry filled with fresh peaches tossed in citrus juice with nutmeg and cinnamon.

review.reviewBody: Okay, after reading about a hundred posts on this recipe, I've taken all the suggestions and put them together to make an excellent Peach Cobbler that was not runny at all. The filling was smooth and luscious! Here's the list: 12-13 peaches (about 4 lbs. I found that 3lbs wasn't enough), 1/2c brown sugar, 1/2c white sugar, 1/4c lemon juice, 1/4c orange juice, 3.5 T cornstarch, 2 tsp vanilla, 1/8 tsp nutmeg, 1 tsp cinnamon, 1 1/2 crust recipe (use only 1 egg and 1/4 c water), and butter instead of shortening. After baking I put it under the broiler for a minute to brown it up a bit. Although the crust/topping was delicious, I might try a more traditional crumb topping next time with flour, oats, butter and brown sugar. I think the ideal combination would be using one recipe of the crust for the bottom, then putting the crumb topping on the top. Both are delicious, it's a matter of what your taste is. Please see my photo.

I thought this recipe was EXCELLENT. I did make a few changes after reading several of the reviews. I did double the crust recipe-it was a bit much-I could have done just fine with a batch and a half. I used a 1/2 cup of shortening and the remaining amount was butter. I used approxiamtely 4lbs of peaches-as far as I'm concerned, you can never use enough fruit in pies. I used 1/4c lemon juice and 1/4 c orange juice. I used 4 tablespoons of cornstarch, one teaspoon of vanilla and a sprinkle of ginger. I also used 1/2 cup of white sugar and 1/2 cup of brown sugar as I used fresh fruit that was sweet enough. I also made the fancy lattice work on the top as suggested by French Blue-it came out gorgeous. I topped mine with some whipped cream and a sprinkle of cinnamon on top. The crust was flakey and delicious and the filling was to die for.....take a look at my picture...and try this recipe!

I wouldn't change much- double the crust, and cook the fruit to get it to the right thickness before making the cobbler. My mama always made extra dough so she could bake several narrow strips while the bottom crust baked. Then as she was adding the filling she would lay those strips throughout the cobbler. Mama made the best and this is as close as I have found. Oh my!!! Hers was a little bit of Heaven in a 9 X 13 baking dish!!!

Consider adding salt if your butter is not salted. I added salt and pure vanilla extract. My peaches were very juicy so I held back 1/4 cup of the liquid. For quick peeling, I drop rinsed peaches in boiling water for a minute. Then transfer peaches into a bowl of ice water. Peel comes off using your fingers.

This actually turned out great for me. I did only a few modifications -- 1.5 tsp pumpkin spice instead of cinnamon and nutmeg, Splenda + Truvia in place of sugar, 1/4 cup of unsalted butter.

I didn't mind that it did come out with more juice. It is a cobbler...not a pie after all. However, I would add an additional tbsp of cornstarch in the future. Nevertheless, using a spoon with holes works well. And, the peaches don't swim in the juices. I'd also use 4 lbs. of peaches.

I have made this cobbler about 20 times or so...with and without homemade crust, also in my conventional oven and my Ninja Foodi Grill Air Fryer and every time, its a hit!! I have made it using more juice because the original peach cobbler tends to have nice slightly thick juice which complements the crust and I have made it dry...I prefer it with the thick juice..I also top it off with Sugar in the Raw to give it a nice crispy crystalized look.

Had a pound of frozen peaches I wanted to use up, so I just adjusted the ingredients for the peaches. I did do the full crust recipe however, and found it just right amount for a full bottom & top crust (no lattice for me) in 8x8 pan. Came out beautifully.

The crust is a little bit of work but worth it, I will use this crust again for other recipes. I have made this several times and everytime I make it for parties people ask for the recipe. There is never leftovers! The only change I made was increasing the cornstarch to 2T. This is a good old fashioned cobbler like my grandmother from KY used to make.

I followed most of the reviews- 1 1/2 dough recipe, 15 peaches, I cut the sugar down to 3/4 c white sugar/ 1/2 c brown sugar, 1/4c lemon juice, 1 cup orangeade (out of juice, dont judge :-) ), 3.5 T cornstarch, 1.5 tsp cinnamon, 1/8 tsp nutmeg. it came out great- a little issue with the pie sides slouching, but it all tasted good.

So yummy! Thanks to all who reviewed and recommended to increase the crust recipe (I made 1-1/2x) and the volume of peaches (I used 4 lbs). In addition, I added about 3/4 blueberries and dusted the top with pecan pieces before baking. It was delicious!
